sections.content:
15,065 people

were counted on the census as "printing machine assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Printing machine assistants set and operate letterpress, platen or cylinder, lithographic and photogravure printing machines, photocopiers, office printers, duplication machines and other reprographic equipment.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "printing machine assistants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "printing machine assistants", 13.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "printing machine assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "printing machine assistants" included:

  • vehicle body builders and repairers
  • metal making and treating process operatives
  • rail transport operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "printing machine assistants" there were more men than women (79.2% compared with 20.8%).

This means "printing machine assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 79.2% and women made up 20.8% of "printing machine assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "printing machine assistants" included:

  • caretakers
  • chemical and related process operatives
  • production managers and directors in manufacturing

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "printing machine assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "printing machine assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "printing machine assistants", 8.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.1% compared with 13.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.9%) than self-employed (6.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
